summary: The two formats themselves are right and I could not break them: I hand-decoded both new goldens byte by byte (BDLT 00000001 03 | seq 09 | count 03 | ... 04 'poda' 05 'inc-a' 04, second segment ends 05, third 00; BCKP 00000001 | ... | 04 'poda' 2a 01 05 'inc-a' 07 d2 09 | 04 'podb' 4d 00) and both match every claim in GoldenAttributedTest's javadoc, including the mixed checkpoint whose second slot's trailing 00 really is the no-pointer flag. Layout selection is by content on both sides (CommitDelta.encode's attribution scan, Checkpoint.encode's anyMatch), so an unattributed object still takes VERSION_DELTA/KIND_DELTA and a pointerless checkpoint still takes v0; the legacy goldens are not staged and theLegacyGoldensAreUnchangedByThisChange pins that. The -1/-1 sentinel is genuinely unrepresentable-by-halves: PodState's compact constructor rejects a half pointer, an incarnation without a pointer and a pointer without an incarnation, and I could not construct one. Version decoding is an enumerated {0,1}. Cost is neutral and I checked it directly: the diff adds no store call at all (the only new reads in capture() are log.epoch() and log.nextSequence(), plain in-memory fields on the commit thread), no LIST, no per-pod request; the checkpoint grows per pod in BYTES only, and the delta by one triple per SEGMENT, which is the axis M4.7 already fixed. What is wrong is the pointer VALUE and the prose the row explicitly owns. MEASURED in a review tree, not inferred: one commitAll of one request produced a delta at epoch 1 sequence 0, and the checkpoint slot for that pod recorded pointer 1/1 -- exactly log.nextSequence(), which observe() reads AFTER log.commitAll has advanced it. Replacing both pointer values with the constants 0/0 leaves :sequencer:test, :format:test and :ingest:test all green, so nothing in the tree constrains the field at all.

findings.title: The pod pointer is written as log.nextSequence() AFTER the commit, so it addresses the slot one PAST the delta that applied -- ADR-0036's pointer is the delta itself
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a review tree: MemoryBinStore, new CommitLog(store,"bins",1), checkpointEveryDeltas=1, one commitAll of CommitRequest("poda","inc-1",0,"seg/a",{RA:3}). The delta was written at epoch 1, sequence 0 (d.sequence()==0). The checkpoint's PodState for poda came back epoch/sequence = 1/1 -- identical to Checkpoint.sequence(), which the record's own javadoc defines as EXCLUSIVE ("the next chain slot NOT covered"). The cause is ordering: LocalSequencer.commitAll calls writer.observe(requests) after log.commitAll, and apply() has already set nextSequence = delta.sequence()+1, so capture()'s `pointerSequence = log.nextSequence()` is last-applied PLUS ONE. ADR-0036 is not ambiguous about what the field means -- "the slot carries a POINTER beside the watermark, (epoch, sequence) of the delta that last applied for that pod", and "read the pointed delta and answer only if it carries that exact (podId, incarnationId, flushSeq)" -- and PodState's new javadoc repeats it ("a POINTER to the delta that last applied", "a slot that looked addressable would answer a replay from the wrong object"). Production consequence, and it is durable: LocalSequencer creates a CheckpointWriter, so every checkpoint this build writes carries a pointer to the wrong object, and those objects sit in the bucket for M4.10d to read. When M4.10d lands, a producer retrying after an ambiguous PUT is detected as a replay, the pointed delta at N+1 is fetched -- it is either absent (the pod's last commit was the newest delta, the overwhelmingly common case for the pod that just committed: one GET of a key that does not exist, then a REFUSE) or it is a LATER, unrelated delta whose triples belong to other flushes (REFUSE again). Criterion 6's "a detected replay is ALWAYS answered" cannot hold for any slot written by this commit, and the lost-ack case M4.10 exists to make safe returns a hard error instead of the original offsets. It also burns one GET per retrying pod on an object that answers nothing. Fix is one line -- carry the sequence of the delta commitAll just returned (or read nextSequence BEFORE the commit) rather than nextSequence after it -- plus an assertion that pins the value.
findings.surviving_mutation: MEASURED green: replace both lines with `long pointerEpoch = 0; long pointerSequence = 0;` and :sequencer:test, :format:test and :ingest:test all pass. Every new assertion on a writer-produced slot checks only lastAppliedFlushSeq, incarnationId().isNotNull() and hasPointer().isTrue() (CheckpointWriterContentTest.java:90-98, :136-140, :157-161, :234-242), and 0/0 satisfies all three -- while PodState's own javadoc says "(0, 0) is a real delta address". No test anywhere compares a slot's epoch/sequence to the sequence of the delta that carried the commit, which is why the off-by-one shipped.

findings.title: The seam prose the row explicitly owns is left standing and is now false: the tree still tells the next session the key is (podId, flushSeq) and that the chain carries no attribution
findings.failure_scenario: The row names these sites and says why in as many words: "AN M4.10d SESSION READS THE SEAM, NOT THIS FILE. Left standing, those javadocs tell it to key dedup on the pair; every M4 fixture is single-incarnation, so the suite stays green while a restarted pod is SUPPRESSED." FakeSequencer's javadoc was updated; the rest were not, including two inside files this commit already edits. Still in the tree after this diff: (1) CheckpointWriter.java:104-106, three lines above the changed code, "it is the only place the writer can see podId and flushSeq, which the chain does not carry" -- the chain now carries all three, and the same class's header still says CommitDelta "carries (sequence, segments) and nothing else, so a new leader cannot recover it", which is the premise ADR-0036 reverses and this commit implements. (2) CommitRequest.java:19-20, "(podId, flushSeq) is the idempotency key M4.10 will use to ignore a replay", and :35-36 "@param flushSeq ... Together with podId it identifies this commit uniquely across the fleet" -- ADR-0036 measured that false, and the new incarnationId component has no @param at all, in a record where every other component has one. (3) Sequencer.java, untouched: ":35 NOT that a given (podId, flushSeq) is applied at most once -- that is M4.10"; ":46 a retry is safe only once the sequencer ignores a replay of a (podId, flushSeq) it has already applied"; ":48-50 The pair is carried from this first commit precisely so M4.10 can make the retry safe without changing the record shape" -- falsified by this very diff, which changes the record shape; ":73-77 neither CommitDelta nor RunCommit carries pod attribution" -- SegmentCommit now does; and ":88 Retrying with the same (podId, flushSeq) is safe only from M4.10". (4) The three descriptive M4/SPEC.md sites the row names by text (line 55 "from the outset -- the commit request carries (podId, flushSeq, segments...)", line 520 Risks row, line 530 the M4.1 row); SPEC.md is not staged at all. (5) wire-format-change's checklist item "the research document that defines the format updated, with a banner if a conclusion changed": 03-metadata-and-cas.md still says "Not carried, deliberately: podId and flushSeq are on the request (CommitRequest) rather than the entry ... it is not in the entry yet, and the Sequencer contract says so in as many words" -- both halves are now false, and that document carries revision banners for ADR-0028 and ADR-0032 precisely so the next reader is not misled. Concrete harm, and it is the row's own argument: the M4.10d author reads Sequencer.java and CheckpointWriter.observe, keys dedup on the pair and recovers the window from the checkpoint only, and every fixture in the tree passes -- CommitProtocolSimulation now hands EVERY pod and EVERY zombie the constant "i1" (:218, :232), and its Issued record at :58 still holds only (podId, flushSeq, segmentKey), so the one simulation that restarts pods cannot see an incarnation at all. Production then suppresses the first commits of every restarted pod, which is the exact failure ADR-0036 exists to prevent.

findings.title: The per-slot presence flag is not an enumerated {0,1}: any other value silently decodes as "no pointer"
findings.failure_scenario: `if (version == VERSION_ATTRIBUTED && c.uvarint() == 1)` treats 0, 2, 7 and 0x1_0000_0001 alike as absent. This class refuses every other value the wire can carry but a record cannot mean -- the version is an enumerated set for exactly this reason, partitionId is range-checked with a measured note about 0x1_0000_0001 narrowing, a repeated pod is refused rather than last-wins -- and the flag is the one new field that is not. A single flipped bit in the flag byte of a v1 checkpoint makes the decoder read the incarnation's length prefix as the NEXT pod's length prefix; the loop then runs podCount times over misaligned bytes and usually dies on the trailing-bytes check with "checkpoint has bytes after its last field", which tells an operator nothing about which field was wrong, and in the tail case where the shifted fields happen to parse it returns a checkpoint with a fabricated pod id and someone else's watermark. One `if (flag != 0 && flag != 1) throw new IOException(...)` costs nothing and matches what the surrounding decoder already does.

findings.title: The write side goes live on deploy with no release in between that can read it, against wire-format-change rule 3
findings.failure_scenario: commitAll now attaches an Attribution unconditionally, so from the first commit after this build starts, EVERY production delta encodes under KIND_DELTA_ATTRIBUTED -- VERSION_DELTA and KIND_DELTA become write-dead. wire-format-change says "readers lag writers by at least one release: ship the read side first, in an earlier commit, then the write side", and here both ship together. During a rolling restart a node still on the previous build that takes the lease hits ChainEntry.decodeKinded's `throw new IOException("unsupported chain entry kind: 3")` while replaying the chain; CheckpointCursor/BinStore define that IOException as "the store is unreachable", so the takeover is refused and the chain has no leader until every node is upgraded. It fails CLOSED rather than corrupting, which is why this is minor and not major, but it is an availability event with a misleading cause, and the tree has an explicit precedent for the opposite order ("A read side that ships first must be no less safe than the one it replaces", CommitLog's seal branch). Worth one sentence in the commit body naming the required rollout order, or a backlog row, rather than a code change now.

findings.title: incarnationId is an unbounded length-prefixed string in both frozen layouts, where ADR-0036 priced it at 16 bytes
findings.failure_scenario: DefaultIngest mints `UUID.randomUUID().toString()`, so the wire carries 36 UTF-8 bytes plus a length prefix, per SEGMENT in every delta and per POD in every checkpoint -- ADR-0036's size argument budgeted "an incarnationId is 16 bytes as a UUID and the pointer two longs, about 32 bytes per pod", so the actual per-pod cost is ~42 bytes, and the per-segment cost in the delta was not priced at all. Nothing caps the length: CommitRequest checks only non-blank, Attribution checks only non-blank, and the decoder bounds incLen against bytes remaining rather than against a maximum, unlike segment keys which have MAX_KEY_BYTES. From M5 this field arrives from a peer over the wire, and a peer sending a 100 KB incarnation inflates every delta PUT and every checkpoint PUT in the window it joins, with the only backstop being a test-only 64 KiB assertion in CheckpointTest that no production path evaluates. The budget is nowhere near breached today (1,600 streams already spend ~38 KiB and pods are few), which is why this is minor -- but the layouts are being frozen in this commit, and a cap is cheap now and a format change later.
